question: How does the national health insurance thing work for foreign students in Korea?
required_facts: International students must subscribe to National Health Insurance (mandatory)
Monthly premium is 79,320 won from March 1, 2026
Not paying disadvantages the immigration review of your extension of stay
Inquiries: 1577-1000 (press 6 for foreign languages)
reference_answer: National Health Insurance is mandatory for international students in Korea. Since March 1, 2026 the monthly premium is 79,320 won, and not paying can hurt the immigration review of your stay extension. For questions call 1577-1000 (press 6 for foreign languages).
notes: Scope default: not an applicant (question not about applying), though persona says applicant. 2025 premium notice kept as outdated.

question: Is there a private insurance option besides the national one? Not sure what the pages say.
required_facts: Yes: the university runs a private/group insurance for international students, separate from NHI
Seoul: enrolled students are paid in full by the university; students who completed coursework pay 25,000 won
ERICA: the 25,000 won premium appears on the tuition bill
reference_answer: Yes. Seoul: Hanyang runs a private insurance separate from NHI; enrolled students are covered by the university budget, and students who completed coursework pay 25,000 won themselves. ERICA: the 25,000 won group-insurance premium is added to your tuition bill.
notes: Campus unstated and the payment route differs; academic_status splits the Seoul answer. Distinct values: university pays vs 25,000 won, so two branches.

question: What documents do I need to prepare before I can do a part-time job?
required_facts: Seoul: Part-time Work Confirmation Form, alien registration card copy, employment contract, business registration copy, transcript or enrollment certificate, language proficiency certificate

ERICA: application form, passport, alien registration card, transcript or attendance certificate, language proficiency proof, confirmation form, business registration copy, standard employment contract
reference_answer: It depends on your campus. At Seoul, prepare the Part-time Work Confirmation Form, a copy of your alien registration card, the employment contract, a business registration copy, your transcript or enrollment certificate and a Korean or English language certificate. At ERICA, you submit the application form, passport, alien registration card, transcript or attendance certificate, language proof, the confirmation form signed by the international-student officer, a business registration copy and the standard employment contract.
notes: Campus unstated; the two campuses list different documents (two branches). Rule is immigration-level but the document checklists are campus-run.

question: Hi, is there some kind of compulsory education that international students must take?
required_facts: Yes: all enrolled international students must complete the 2026 Mandatory Education online
Deadline: Sunday, September 13, 2026
reference_answer: Yes. All enrolled international students must complete the 2026 Mandatory Education online by Sunday, September 13, 2026, through the link in the OIA notice.
notes: Only Seoul evidence; ERICA search found nothing. Deadline already passed at snapshot date (2026-11-10) but the obligation is the stable fact; caveat.

question: What is the psychological health test for international students and why is it done?
required_facts: It is a short PHQ-9 test that checks your mental health over the past two weeks
Purpose: to check in on your mental health and connect to a counselor if support seems needed
Results are confidential and participation is voluntary
reference_answer: It is a short PHQ-9 questionnaire that gives a simple overview of how you have felt over the past two weeks. OIA offers it so students can check in on their mental health and be contacted by a counselor if extra support seems needed. Results are confidential and taking it is voluntary; the notice lists international undergraduate and graduate students at Seoul as eligible.
notes: Gold persona is non_degree; the notice lists undergrad/grad only, handled as a caveat. 2025 notices say the same; the March 2026 one is used.

question: How can I sign up for counseling services as an international student?
required_facts: Seoul: visit OIA or e-mail, fill in the application form, take an interview or test, then counseling
Seoul contact: 02-2220-2450, International Building room 218, Mon-Fri 9-5
ERICA: HY-in > Application > Personal Counseling/Psychological Testing, or call 031-400-4926
reference_answer: At Seoul, visit the OIA or e-mail, fill in the application form and take an interview or test before counseling starts (02-2220-2450, International Building room 218, Mon-Fri 9-5). At ERICA, book through HY-in > Application > Personal Counseling/Psychological Testing.
notes: Campus unstated and booking routes differ; two branches.

question: Tell me about the International Winter School, what is it about?
required_facts: Hanyang International Winter School (HIWS) offers 130+ courses in 12 disciplines taught in English
Two different 2-week sessions to choose from
Scholarships, e.g. 40% tuition discount (Active Partner Scholarship); cultural activities and buddy program
reference_answer: The Hanyang International Winter School at the Seoul campus offers 130+ English-taught courses across 12 disciplines in two 2-week sessions. Scholarships such as a 40% Active Partner discount are available, and the program includes six cultural activities and a buddy program.
notes: Description page, no dates or fees in the snapshot (not asked).

question: What makes Hanyang's International Summer School worth joining?
required_facts: Choose up to 3 courses at a flat fee from 130+ English-taught courses
Scholarships including a 40% Active Partner discount
Global network of 2000+ students from 45+ nationalities; cultural activities and buddy program
reference_answer: HISS lets you pick up to 3 of 130+ English-taught courses for a flat fee, offers scholarships including a 40% Active Partner discount, brings together 2000+ students from 45+ nationalities, and adds cultural activities, a buddy program and research opportunities.
notes: Marketing page; answer is the listed selling points.

question: Difference between exchange student program and the visiting student program?
required_facts: Exchange: students nominated by partner universities study 1-2 semesters as fee-waived students
Visiting: fee-paying program open to international students for 1-2 semesters
reference_answer: Exchange students are officially nominated by a partner university and study one or two semesters as fee-waived students. The Visiting Student Program is fee-paying and open to international students who want to take courses for one or two semesters.
notes: ERICA has its own exchange pages; question not campus-specific and gold is Seoul.

question: how do I apply for scholarships
required_facts: HIEA: apply online yourself through the HY-in portal (International Students > International Scholarship Application), in set windows each semester
Other scholarships (e.g. TOPIK scholarship, Samsung Global Hope) have their own notices and windows; Samsung documents go to the OIA, room 218
reference_answer: Apply through each scholarship notice. For the HIEA you apply yourself online: log in to the HY-in portal, open International Students > International Scholarship Application, select the semester and click Apply for Scholarship. Other scholarships such as the TOPIK scholarship or the Samsung Global Hope Scholarship have their own windows; Samsung documents go to the OIA in International Building room 218. Each has its own GPA and language conditions.
notes: Gold is Seoul; campus unstated but ERICA also applies via HY-in, so same procedure. Windows quoted are 2026-1; the procedure is the stable part.

question: Where is the Office of International Affairs and how can I reach them?
required_facts: Seoul: OIA, International Building, 222 Wangsimri-ro, Seongdong-gu; Tel +82-2-2220-2453~2460
ERICA: OIA, 3F Student Welfare Building, 55 Hanyangdaehak-ro, Ansan; 031-400-0791~0795; weekdays 8:30-17:30 in semester
reference_answer: At Seoul, the OIA is in the International Building, 222 Wangsimri-ro, Seongdong-gu (tel +82-2-2220-2453~2460). At ERICA, it is on the 3F of the Student Welfare Building, 55 Hanyangdaehak-ro, Ansan (tel 031-400-0791~0795; weekdays 8:30-17:30 in semester).
notes: Campus unstated; two offices. Seoul Contact Us says room #108 while the counseling page says #218 (different offices); not used.

question: What are Hanyang's international rankings and how many international students study here?
required_facts: Seoul: QS subject rankings (e.g. Architecture 54th, Chemical Engineering 53rd) and 3,188 degree-seeking international students
ERICA: QS World University Rankings 164th (2024) and 4,500+ international students (as of July 2023)
reference_answer: Seoul campus pages list QS subject rankings (Architecture 54th, Chemical Engineering 53rd, Civil 60th, Mechanical 57th, Materials 58th) and 3,188 degree-seeking international students. ERICA lists QS World University Ranking 164th (2024) and more than 4,500 international students (July 2023). The figures may be outdated.
notes: Hard: Seoul table is garbled and undated; ERICA figures are 2023/2024. Treated as campus branch (different figures).

question: Does the university run drug prevention education?
required_facts: Yes: drug prevention education was held for international students enrolled in degree programs (2026-08)
All international students are advised to review the materials in the attached file
reference_answer: Yes. Hanyang drug prevention supporters gave a drug prevention education session for degree-program international students, and all international students are advised to review the attached materials and avoid any drug-related crime.
notes: Gold persona is non_degree; the session targeted degree students but the advice is for all (caveat).

question: Any safety advice for crowded places this season?
required_facts: Avoid crowded areas such as Itaewon, Hongdae and Seongsu; stay away from narrow alleys and stairways
If a crowd builds up move away when safe, follow police instructions; call 112 or 119 in an emergency
reference_answer: Avoid heavily crowded areas such as Itaewon, Hongdae and Seongsu, stay away from narrow alleys and stairways, leave a crowd that suddenly grows once it is safe, follow police instructions, and call 112 (police) or 119 (fire/ambulance) in an emergency. The OIA notice was written for Halloween (October 31, 2026).
notes: Event-specific notice; general precautions treated as stable. No ERICA equivalent found.

question: What does the OIA do for international students?
required_facts: OIA is the liaison between Hanyang and the global community and runs study abroad, exchange, short-term and degree programs, summer and winter schools
OIA offers counseling for international students (individual, group, psychological testing)
reference_answer: The Seoul OIA links Hanyang with the global community and runs programs such as study abroad, exchange, short and long-term study, and the International Summer and Winter Schools. For international students it also provides counseling, including individual and group counseling and psychological testing.
notes: Broad question; answer built from the greeting and counseling pages.

question: Is there a free Korean class run by volunteers?
required_facts: Yes: ISF (International Student Fellowship) volunteers run a free Korean class every semester
Held every Tuesday evening; first 20 students; pre-application through the Google link
reference_answer: Yes. The International Student Fellowship (ISF), a volunteer group, runs a free Korean class each semester on Tuesday evenings for the first 20 applicants; complete the pre-application form linked in the OIA notice.
notes: Notice from 2026-03 (spring); the class is described as every semester.

question: What is the GKS-G university track and what forms does it need?
required_facts: University track: fill in the online form, then submit documents in person or by post to OIA, International Building #218
Forms include application form, personal statement, study plan, recommendation letter, applicant agreement, medical assessment and consent form
Screening, then a Zoom interview for those passing document screening
reference_answer: The GKS-G university track is the Global Korea Scholarship graduate-degree application handled by Hanyang itself. You fill in the online form, submit the documents in person or by post to the OIA (International Building #218), and those who pass document screening have a Zoom interview. Required forms include the application form, personal statement, study plan, a recommendation letter, applicant agreement, medical assessment and consent form, plus degree certificates and transcripts.
notes: Dates are from the 2026 round (Feb-Mar 2026), already closed; 2025 round kept as outdated. Persona is non_degree; graduate-degree scholarship noted as caveat.

question: Where can I see the regular admission results for international students?
required_facts: Admission results are on the OIA "Regular Admission Results" page (separate Undergraduate and Graduate links)
reference_answer: Open the OIA website’s “Regular Admission Results” page; it has separate links for undergraduate and graduate admission results.
notes: Only the page title and links are in the snapshot; the result lists themselves are not.

question: What facilities does the ERICA dorm have besides rooms?
required_facts: Open Space Zone, activity room (table tennis, darts) and practice rooms for instruments and singing, all open 09:00-24:00
Residential college cafeteria (KRW 3,500 per meal)
reference_answer: ERICA’s dorm has an Open Space Zone, an activity room with table tennis and darts, musical instrument and singing practice rooms (09:00-24:00), and a cafeteria at KRW 3,500 per meal.
notes: Question names ERICA.

question: Is there a bank or post office near the ERICA campus?
required_facts: Shinhan Bank and the campus post office are on 1F of the Student Welfare Building, open Mon-Fri 09:00-16:00
reference_answer: Yes. Both are on the ERICA campus, on the 1F of the Student Welfare Building: Shinhan Bank (031-419-2203) and the post office next to it (031-406-2004), open Monday to Friday 09:00-16:00.
notes: Question names ERICA.

question: What kind of events or programs does ERICA offer to support international students?
required_facts: Field programs 1-2 times per semester
K-Movie Night with free tickets
Hanmille peer mentoring (new year-1 undergraduates and new postgraduates apply as mentees)
GLOBAL LOVE HYU, a 1-year program with up to KRW 1,000,000 scholarship
reference_answer: ERICA’s OIA runs field programs (1-2 per semester), K-Movie Night with free tickets, the Hanmille peer mentoring program (mentee spots go to new year-1 undergraduates and new postgraduates) and GLOBAL LOVE HYU, a one-year group with a scholarship of up to KRW 1,000,000.
notes: Question names ERICA. Mentoring eligibility is a caveat for the language-program persona.

question: What scholarships exist at ERICA?
required_facts: Hanyang International Excellence Awards (HIEA): 30-100% of one semester tuition
TOPIK Scholarship: KRW 500,000-1,000,000 for improving your TOPIK level
Both have eligibility conditions (GPA, valid TOPIK, exclusions)
reference_answer: The ERICA scholarship page lists the Hanyang International Excellence Awards (30%, 50%, 70% or 100% of one semester of tuition) and the TOPIK Scholarship (KRW 500,000 or 1,000,000 when your TOPIK level improves). Each has conditions, e.g. GPA and a valid TOPIK score for HIEA, and exclusions such as students on leave or completed students for the TOPIK scholarship.
notes: Question names ERICA. The persona (master, completed coursework) may be excluded; stated as caveat.

question: Who can I talk to if I feel really down while studying here?
required_facts: Seoul: the OIA counseling program (visit or e-mail, 02-2220-2450, International Building, Mon-Fri 9-5; English available)
ERICA: the counseling center for international students, 031-400-4926 (English, Korean), HY-in booking; 24-hour help 1577-1366 or 112 in a crisis
reference_answer: At Seoul, talk to the OIA counseling program (visit or e-mail; 02-2220-2450, International Building, weekdays 9-5; counseling in English is available). At ERICA, use the counseling center for international students (031-400-4926 English/Korean, weekdays 10-17, bookable on HY-in); in a crisis call 1577-1366 or 112, available 24 hours.
notes: Question does not name the campus; contacts differ. Persona is ERICA but the stated profile has no campus.

question: do you do personal counseling and psychological tests?
required_facts: Yes: ERICA offers 1-on-1 personal counseling (up to 12 sessions) and psychological testing for international students
Free and confidential, in English, Chinese and Korean
reference_answer: Yes. ERICA’s counseling center for international students offers 1-on-1 personal counseling (up to 12 sessions of 45 minutes) and psychological tests such as MMPI-2, MBTI and FCPI, in English, Chinese or Korean, confidentially.
notes: Campus unstated; both campuses say yes, details differ but are not asked. Seoul span placed as inapplicable.

question: Any group counseling or workshops for students?
required_facts: Yes: ERICA runs group counseling on communication skills, relationships and procrastination
One-off workshops (DIY handicrafts, meditation, color therapy), 2 per semester
reference_answer: Yes. ERICA offers group counseling on topics such as communication skills, personal relationships and procrastination, and one-off workshops (handicrafts, meditation, color therapy) twice a semester.
notes: Campus unstated; both say yes. Seoul span inapplicable for the ERICA gold profile.

question: What does the university group insurance cover?
required_facts: Covers death from injury or disease, medical expenses for injury or sickness, personal liability, overseas hospitalization and special expenses for foreigners
Not covered: non-reimbursable items such as manual therapy, shock wave therapy, injections, MRI/MRA
reference_answer: The ERICA university group insurance covers death from injury or disease and its aftereffects, reimbursable and non-reimbursable medical expenses for injury or sickness, personal liability, overseas hospitalization and medical expenses, and special expenses for foreigners. The listed non-reimbursable expenses include manual therapy, shock wave therapy, proliferation therapy, injections and MRI/MRA.
notes: Only ERICA gives coverage details; Seoul page has none, so no campus branch. Page lists non-reimbursable items under the coverage heading.

question: What is alien registration and when do I have to do it?
required_facts: Foreigners staying more than 90 days must register as aliens
Register within 90 days of entry; failing leads to a fine
reference_answer: Alien registration is the registration of foreigners who stay in Korea for more than 90 days. You must apply within 90 days of entering the country, or immediately when you receive a residency status; missing the deadline can result in a fine.
notes: National rule on an ERICA page; applies to the D-4 gold student.

question: Can you explain the group visa application process?
required_facts: Group applications are announced in each semester’s registration notices
The step-by-step group visa process is only in the attached guide, which has no extracted text

inapplicable_evidence.why: Seoul undergraduate acceptance guideline; gold student is at ERICA

reference_answer: ERICA announces group registrations in its notices each semester, but the step-by-step process is only in the attached guide of the ERICA notice, which the snapshot cannot read. Check the ERICA OIA notice or ask the ERICA OIA.
notes: Campus unstated, gold ERICA. Seoul explains group visas for new undergraduates; ERICA only in an attachment. partial because the notice-each-semester fact is supported.

question: Why study at ERICA instead of the main campus?
required_facts: ERICA is a hub for industry-academia collaboration (143 companies on campus)
Large and international: 10,000+ undergraduate students and 4,500+ international students; 600 partner universities
reference_answer: ERICA presents itself as Korea’s most active campus for industry-academia cooperation, with 143 companies on campus, 10,000+ undergraduates and 4,500+ international students, and 600 partner universities in 70 countries. The pages do not compare it directly with the main campus.
notes: Comparison with the Seoul campus is not in the snapshot; answered with ERICA’s own claims. Figures dated July 2023.

question: What are outgoing programs and what are the benefits?
required_facts: Outgoing programs let you study at a partner university abroad while paying tuition to Hanyang
Credits earned abroad can be transferred back to Hanyang
reference_answer: Outgoing programs let you study for a period at a partner university abroad under an exchange agreement while paying tuition to Hanyang; the credits you earn can be transferred to Hanyang when you return.
notes: The page has an Advantages heading with no extracted text; benefits taken from the definition. ERICA pages; Seoul has no outgoing page found. A graduating doctoral student may be ineligible (not asked).

question: Can I get a scholarship?
required_facts: Which scholarships you can get depends on campus (Seoul vs ERICA lists differ), degree level and TOPIK level
Seoul examples: HIEA (GPA 3.0 undergraduate / 4.2 graduate, TOPIK or IELTS/TOEFL), TOPIK scholarship (TOPIK level 5 or 6)

inapplicable_evidence.why: ERICA scholarship list; gold student is at Seoul

reference_answer: Which campus are you at (Seoul or ERICA)? The scholarships and conditions differ by campus, degree level and TOPIK level. At Seoul, for example, a doctoral student with TOPIK level 5 could look at the TOPIK scholarship and the HIEA (graduate GPA 4.2).
notes: Hard: open question, several vocabulary attributes split the evidence (more than two distinct answers), so clarify on campus, the biggest split. GPA, nationality and DAC list are caveats outside the vocabulary.

question: How do I take a break from my studies and come back later?
required_facts: Seoul: leave is granted one year at a time; if you do not re-register when it ends you are dismissed; applications are not accepted in person or by e-mail
ERICA: apply through HY-in > Application > Leave of Absence, and leave Korea within 30 days; one year at a time, up to 3 years for undergraduates
reference_answer: It depends on your campus. At Seoul, leave is granted one year at a time, you must re-register when it ends or you are dismissed, and applications by visit or e-mail are not accepted. At ERICA, apply online through HY-in > Application > Leave of Absence; you must leave Korea within 30 days, and undergraduates can take up to 1 year at a time and 3 years in total.
notes: Campus unstated; windows quoted are 2026 terms, procedures are the stable part. Seoul leave application path itself is only in a notice, so Seoul facts come from the policy note.

question: Do I have to join the national health insurance?
required_facts: Yes: National Health Insurance is mandatory for international students
Not paying disadvantages your extension of stay review
reference_answer: Yes. Subscription to National Health Insurance is mandatory for international students, and not paying it can count against you when immigration reviews your extension of stay. The premium is 79,320 won a month since March 2026.
notes: T14-109 style: no evidence splits by visa or student type. Visiting students not exempted in any page.

question: How do I extend my stay? My card expires soon.
required_facts: Apply from 4 months before the visa expiry date, no later than the expiry date
Documents: application form, passport copy, alien registration card, certificate of enrollment, tuition receipt, last transcript, proof of residence, fee KRW 60,000
Stay in Korea until the extension is approved
reference_answer: Apply at the immigration office from 4 months before your visa expires, and no later than the expiry date. Bring the application form, passport copy, alien registration card, certificate of enrollment, tuition receipt, last semester transcript and proof of residence, and pay KRW 60,000. Stay in Korea until the extension is approved. The Seoul Immigration Office has moved to 55 Jeongui-ro, Songpa-gu since 2026-10-19.
notes: Immigration rule from the ERICA page used for a Seoul student (national). Extra bank-balance or supervisor documents apply only in special cases (GPA below 2.0, extra semester): caveat.

question: Can the school apply for my visa for me?
required_facts: In principle you apply for the D-2 visa and residence card yourself at the immigration office
The OIA gives you the Certificate of Admission and offers a group visa application for convenience
Overseas applicants get the visa at an embassy
reference_answer: Not fully. The rule is that you apply for the D-2 visa and residence card yourself at the immigration office or an embassy, but the OIA issues your Certificate of Admission and offers group visa applications for students in Korea to make it easier.
notes: Persona is an applicant (scope default for the visa-after-admission context); the question does not state it. Uses the Seoul 2026 undergraduate acceptance guideline.

question: Do I have to file an entry report when I arrive?
required_facts: Yes: all international degree students must respond to the entry and exit report on HY-in every semester
Students on leave or not yet in Korea must also respond
Not responding can cost you your immigration status (visa cancellation, entry refusal)
reference_answer: Yes. All international degree students must respond to the entry and exit report on the HY-in portal every semester, including students on leave or not yet in Korea, and update it when things change. Not responding can lead to visa cancellation or entry refusal.
notes: Latest notices are from 2022; the rule is stable and no newer version exists. Older 2021 notice not added to outdated_evidence.

question: Do I need a TOPIK score to study here?
required_facts: Degree students must meet the Korean standard: TOPIK level 4 or higher or Hanyang IIE level 4
Whether exchange or visiting students need TOPIK is not stated in the snapshot
reference_answer: For degree programs you need to meet the Korean standard (TOPIK level 4 or higher, or Hanyang IIE level 4); otherwise you take a leave for the first semester. The pages I found do not say whether exchange or visiting students need a TOPIK score, so please ask the Seoul OIA.
notes: Hard: question is generic; gold is an exchange student, for whom no page states a TOPIK rule, so partial. Evidence is the 2026 undergraduate acceptance guideline. English-track exemptions are not shown in the snapshot text.

question: Do I have to take that psychological test?
required_facts: No: taking the Psychological Health Test is voluntary
Results are confidential and only a counseling professional reviews them
reference_answer: No. The Psychological Health Test is voluntary; take it only if you are comfortable. Your results are confidential and only a counselor sees them.
notes: “That psychological test” read as the Seoul Psychological Health Test. 2023 notice (asks everyone to take it) kept as outdated. Gold persona is an applicant and the test is for enrolled Seoul students (caveat).

question: Is the compulsory education mandatory for me?
required_facts: All enrolled international students must complete the 2026 Mandatory Education by September 13, 2026
The notice does not say whether students on leave of absence must take it
reference_answer: The 2026 notice says all enrolled international students must complete the Mandatory Education online by September 13, 2026. It does not say whether students on a leave of absence are included, so ask the Seoul OIA.
notes: Unknown condition for leave students treated as caveat, not a branch (9.3). Deadline already passed at snapshot date.

question: Am I eligible for the GKS scholarship?
required_facts: The GKS-G in the snapshot is for graduate degrees; you need a bachelor’s degree (or be expected to graduate by July 31, 2026)
Citizenship of a GKS-designated country, parents not Korean citizens, under 40 years old, CGPA at least 80% or 2.64/4.0
A year-3 undergraduate does not yet hold the required degree
reference_answer: The GKS-G in the Hanyang notices is a graduate-degree scholarship. You need a bachelor’s degree (or expected graduation by July 31, 2026), citizenship of a designated country with non-Korean parents, to be under 40 and meet the CGPA threshold. As a year-3 undergraduate exchange student you do not yet qualify for the graduate program. The 2026 round is closed and no newer round is published.
notes: Hard: question says only “GKS”; snapshot has only GKS-G. degree_level is not made a branch because out-of-vocabulary criteria (nationality, age, GPA) decide most of the answer; clarify is acceptable.
